card.band: 4 h. Narrow, but it needs a real C++ build and profiling. Frontier agents get the main fix in some trials, but the secondary hotspots limit the average. Weaker models stall on the build.
card.cheat: Persisting an index file between runs is closed because each run starts from fresh packs. The file-tree equality gate catches dropped override semantics.
card.grading: Hard gate: the resulting virtual file tree and the bytes read must be identical on generated packs, plus a conflicting-override test. Score is the median speedup on hidden pack sizes and layouts.
card.reference: The upstream fix measured on the same harness, which sets the ceiling.
card.task: /app ships Godot's PCK/file-access and resource-pack code at the pinned base. The agent speeds up loading of a patch pack over a base pack with a very large file table (hundreds of thousands of entries), covering directory registration, path normalisation and lookup. A headless harness builds packs with the packer and times the load.
card.title: Godot patch PCK loading slowdown on large projects

history: No strong reference obtainable for the seed as written: the public fix (PR #105984) is an Android export-format change, not a loader speedup, and was never measured on a headless pack harness; the reference would have to be built by us, and the Linux hotspot is unverified.

facts.claim: Godot issue #102998 exists and is titled 'Loading patch PCK on Android with big project is slow'; closed as completed on 2025-06-25
The reported slowdown is Android-specific: it runs through DirAccessJAndroid (dir_exists, current_is_dir) and android::ZipAssetsProvider, not generic PCK loading on desktop
The seed's framing (generic patch-pack over base-pack load, path normalisation and lookup, timed by a headless harness) matches the upstream incident
Upstream fix PR #105984 ('Android: Implement sparse bundle PCK support') was merged on 2025-06-25 into master, milestone 4.5
The upstream fix changes the export format: a {name}.sparsepck header/directory plus hashed sibling files, which is an export-side change rather than a loader speedup on a given pack
Upstream PR #105984 reports load time dropping from 8570 ms to 10 ms on its minimal reproduction
PR #105984 file count and additions/deletions (needed to check the 150+ line reference requirement)
A headless harness that builds packs with the packer and times the load exists in the repo or anywhere public
Repository is MIT licensed, C++, stars 118744, release 4.7.2-stable (as given in source_facts; not re-fetched)
Smoke build verdict for the source (seed smoke_build is empty, so no offline build or test result exists)

spike_plan.kill_if: The build takes over a day, or the Linux load shows no hotspot distinct from I/O, so no reference can be measured on the seed's harness
spike_plan.pass_if: Template builds offline and a measurable hotspot in patch load (directory registration or lookup) appears on Linux with hundreds of thousands of entries
steps: Clone godotengine/godot at the parent commit of PR #105984 into a throwaway container with network; do not keep history for the bundle
Build the Linux editor-free export template with scons (target=template_release, 8 jobs) and time it
Generate a base PCK and a patch PCK with ~200k-entry file tables using the packer (pck export or a script writing the PCK format)
Time ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack on the patch over the base, 5 runs each, and profile with gprof or perf-free sampling to see whether PackedSourceDirectory::try_open_pack dominates
Check whether the reported slowdown reproduces on Linux at all; if not, the headless harness does not match the incident
Repeat the build and timing twice to check determinism of the tree and bytes read

v1.summary: The seed's source issue #102998 is real and fixed upstream by merged PR #105984, but the reported slowdown is Android-specific (Kotlin directory checks) and the fix changes the export format to a sparse bundle, so the seed's generic headless-harness framing does not match it. Killed as K5: no reference can be obtained for the seed as written, and the public fix is directly visible in git history, which would need a history-less snapshot.
